d.description:
eCash is a Bitcoin hard fork initiated by Bitcoin developer Paul Sztorc. The project aims to preserve Bitcoin's core architecture while introducing native support for Drivechains (BIP-300) and additional Layer 2 functionality.

The network is designed as a near-copy of Bitcoin Core, using the SHA-256 proof-of-work algorithm and maintaining compatibility with the existing Bitcoin software stack wherever practical. Bitcoin holders will be able to claim eCash on a 1:1 basis after the fork.

The project's objective is to provide an alternative Bitcoin-compatible network focused on experimentation with scalability, programmable sidechains, and protocol development while preserving the familiar Bitcoin user experience.

eCash is an open-source project. Development is led by Paul Sztorc, the creator of the Drivechain proposal, with source code, technical documentation, and development updates published publicly. The project seeks to enable innovation through optional Layer 2 networks while maintaining a simple and transparent Layer 1 protocol.
d.short_description: eCash is a Bitcoin hard fork that preserves its core architecture while adding native support for BIP-300

tasks.title: Getting $pECX
tasks.description_html:
eCash announced  the launch of the Alpha phase. You can receive $pECX test tokens for holding $BTC in your wallets until block 963,648, and in the future, once the relevant functionality becomes available, burn them to receive $ECX tokens.

Alpha stage was launched on August 23, 2026, at block 963,648. The first snapshot was taken at that very moment
If you hold $BTC in a non-custodial wallet at the time of the snapshot, you are eligible to receive $pECX

Important
• On October 31, 2026, at the time of the mainnet launch, a separate, new snapshot will be taken
• All BTC holders included in this snapshot will automatically receive $ECX tokens at a 1:1 ratio
• The $pECX burn is an additional bonus for early users - you will receive these tokens in addition to the main 1:1 airdrop, not instead of it

Burn and Conversion Mechanics:
• At this time, the feature to convert $pECX to $ECX has not been added to the current version of the eCash wallet. Currently, the interface only allows you to claim $pECX. The conversion button will appear in future updates.
• During the Alpha stage through September 20, 2026, the conversion rate is: 1 $pECX = 0.01 $ECX
• During the Beta phase, starting September 20, 2026, the rate will be more favorable: 1 $pECX = 0.02 $ECX


1. Go to the website and download the eCash wallet installation package

 

2. Install the wallet on the device of your choice and select the "Light" type

4. Enter your seed phrase and continue creating your wallet

 

5. Confirm the creation of the wallet

 

6. Select the Alphanet network

 

7. To complete the following steps, you'll need to copy the private key for your BTC wallet
Example using a UniSat wallet:

 

 

8. After you’ve copied the key, open your eCash wallet and go to the “Receive” section
Before proceeding to the next step, you can withdraw your BTC from wallet to another one if you’re concerned about the safety of your funds. 
Importing a private key is safe for your main assets: it does not convert your $BTC, but merely grants the eCash wallet access to $pECX test coins created for your address at the time of the snapshot

 

9. Insert the key and press the mint button. You will then receive $pECX, which you can later convert to $ECX

d.description:
Ekiden is an institutional-grade, orderbook-based hybrid derivatives exchange built natively for the Canton Network ecosystem. Designed to meet the stringent demands of high-frequency traders and financial institutions, the platform combines the speed of off-chain matching with the transparency of delayed on-chain settlement. This unique rollup-like architecture empowers users to execute complex trading strategies with deep liquidity while eliminating traditional counterparty risks.

Functioning as a seamless decentralized trading terminal, the ecosystem bridges the gap between centralized execution and decentralized finance. The application provides professionals with robust API connectivity, cross-chain access, and advanced market structures. Recently approved as a Featured App on Canton, the project delivers a secure, compliant, and highly efficient environment for the next generation of tokenized asset trading.

d.description:
Arc is an open Layer-1 blockchain designed to provide an enterprise-grade foundation for stablecoin payments, FX, and capital markets applications. The EVM-compatible network features USDC as its native gas, along with an integrated stablecoin FX engine, sub-second settlement finality, and opt-in privacy controls. Arc will be fully integrated across Circle’s platform and services, which will also remain fully available and interoperable with the dozens of other partner blockchains that Circle supports.

Featuring:

  • USDC as native gas

  • Built-in FX engine

  • Deterministic sub-second finality

  • Opt-in privacy

  • Full Circle platform integration

At its core is Malachite, a high-performance consensus engine developed by Informal Systems that powers Arc with safety, liveness, and resilience at scale.

Arc expands the design space for stablecoins by uniting speed with certainty and delivering the native tooling needed to meet real-world business obligations. Open and composable, Arc is designed to interoperate seamlessly with the broader multichain ecosystem. Fully EVM-compatible, developers will be able to build on Arc using the same frameworks and tooling they know and trust.
d.short_description: ARC is an EVM-compatible Layer-1 blockchain by Circle for stablecoin finance, featuring USDC as a gas token and a built-in FX engine.

d.description:
Miden is a zero-knowledge (ZK) rollup layer 2 blockchain designed to enhance blockchain scalability, privacy, and security by shifting transaction execution and state management to the client side. This approach allows users to generate and verify their own transactions locally, reducing the need for re-execution on the main chain. By enabling client-side proving, Miden aims to alleviate the computational burden on the network, facilitating more efficient and scalable decentralized applications.​

In terms of privacy, Miden's architecture empowers users with full control over their data and transaction details through self-custodied state management. Security is bolstered by supporting smart contract development in Rust and incorporating built-in account abstraction. Additionally, native asset storage for user accounts minimizes the attack surface, enhancing overall system robustness.

d.description:
Quip Network is a base layer protocol that adds post-quantum security to existing blockchains and forms decentralized infrastructure for quantum computing workloads.

It introduces QUIPs as secure, composable transaction inputs like enhanced lockboxes that wrap classical assets with post-quantum signatures using algorithms like WOTS+ to protect against future quantum attacks.

Users depositing funds into QUIP-enabled contracts or wallets, creating states for proposals, approvals, claims, and timeouts that allow atomic cross-network operations without altering underlying chains.

Key components include:

  • Integrates seamlessly with networks like Bitcoin or Ethereum via wallet extensions or smart contracts, maintaining compatibility without protocol changes.

  • QUIP token for incentives in validation, staking, nominations, and quantum job execution;

  • validators (full nodes) and canary nodes (lightweight attestation);

  • quantum clusters that run verifiable quantum tasks (e.g., hash mining, key recovery) using classical or quantum processors.

The protocol supports portable, liquid, and programmable assets across chains, with features like staking, swaps, flash loans, and zero-knowledge proofs embedded in QUIPs. It incentivizes reporting of quantum vulnerabilities through emissions and creates a mechanism to distribute attack costs via verifiable proofs. Overall, it combines post-quantum cryptography overlays with a shared quantum compute layer for both security enhancements and workload acceleration.
d.short_description: Quip is a post-quantum security layer and shared quantum compute network for blockchains.
